verbatims.quote: A 0 to 100 'who the data likes' number is a tip with a progress bar. App Review and our RG team would both read it that way.
The market already has a number for each side. It's called the price. If your score disagrees with the line, I'd want to know why before anyone trusts it.
ATS records and four-game streaks are mostly noise. Start Here is fine for casuals, but sharp guys won't open an app for it.
The score is the hook. People screenshot a 78 vs 22. That's what drives installs.
Start Here is basically my show prep. Three facts I can say on air in 20 seconds.
Four books refreshed a few times a day is thin. Line movement that's hours stale near kickoff won't impress anyone serious.
Side-by-Side is the cleanest. It's what our own game pages try to do, and users still scroll past half of it.
The AI analyst is the bigger legal question. 'Won't tell you what to bet' has to hold up when someone asks 'who wins tonight' fifty different ways.

researcher_note: Start Here top Q1 (70 vs 66) and best usefulness. Score splits hardest: 23/250 trust as is, 71 risk flags (more than other three combined), 105 say lowers trust. Analyst 36 flags: compliance doubts guardrail holds under probing.
